policy.reason: An agent may record the session it is working in, because that is the point: footage of the work it just did, to be edited into a tutorial afterwards. `targetsSession` means the bus has already established that this session belongs to the caller, so 'record a session' can only ever mean 'record my own'. The recording is a file in the owner's own home — never uploaded, never sent to a model — so producing it does not cross the boundary that ISessionVisionConsent exists to hold; anything that later SENDS one somewhere does, and must ask separately. Two limits are structural rather than advisory: a hard duration ceiling passed to ffmpeg itself, so a runtime that dies without stopping cannot leave a process filling the home volume, and an on-screen recording marker, because a person may take a seat at a session that is already recording and must be able to see that without being told.

Ending a recording of one's own session takes nothing away and removes the on-screen marker. It reports a SHORT file as a failure rather than a success: ffmpeg exits 0 after the X display is resized out from under it — which is what happens when a viewer connects — so the encoded duration is the only honest witness that the footage is whole.
